A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original heuristic-generation experiments, candidate-count sensitivity analysis, and planning results on 720 test tasks across eight domains.

after.justification: V2 retains original planning experiments and adds end-to-end LLM comparisons, prompt ablations, altered and novel domain tests, and runtime analysis.

M1.justification: Both versions generate candidate Python heuristics, evaluate them with GBFS, select by training coverage with an agile-score tie-breaker, and reuse the selected heuristic. The Blocksworld and Spanner code listings are unchanged. Expanded documentation and additional evaluated models do not establish a change to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 retains the eight IPC domains and adds reusable-spanner dynamics, Blocksworld with randomly renamed symbols, and the new Rod-Rings domain. These extend evaluation to changed action semantics, obfuscated inputs, and a distinct planning domain.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds direct end-to-end planning with Gemini Flash, Flash Thinking, DeepSeek V3, and R1 as evaluated comparators. Table 3 additionally includes V3-generated heuristics in the Fast Downward comparison. The existing classical and learned heuristic baselines remain.

E3.justification: New protocols include one LLM call per test task with VAL validation, ablations evaluating all 25 candidates under five-minute limits, and additional o3 configurations. Appendix E measures expansions per second on jointly solved tasks, excluding preprocessing. The main selected-heuristic evaluation retains its 30-minute/8-GiB limits.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's candidate-count analysis, v2 adds eight prompt-component ablations, tests probing memorization through modified, obfuscated, and novel domains, and a cross-planner throughput analysis. These examine prompt dependence, generalization mechanisms, selection quality, and implementation efficiency.

E5.justification: Table 4 newly reports standard deviations of candidate performance and specifies exclusion of failed heuristics from average coverage. V1 reports averages without comparable dispersion reporting. This characterizes candidate variability; it does not establish repeated full-pipeline experiments or uncertainty estimates for the headline comparisons.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces V3's total coverage of 283 with 343, changing its ranking; v2 specifies version 0324 while v1 leaves the version unspecified, so this is not an established same-configuration gain. R1's 373 and Pyperplan hFF's 243 remain unchanged. V2 adds direct-planning, ablation, robustness, o3, and throughput results, while removing the original per-model failure rates and detailed sampling curve.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds limited theoretical assertions, including Miconic's 2-approximability, Sokoban's PSPACE-completeness, and the claim that the selected Sokoban heuristic cannot overestimate optimal plan length. The core planning assumptions and agile-score formula remain unchanged; no new proofs are supplied.

C1.justification: V2 adds the explicit headline claim that heuristic generation solves more tasks overall than direct LLM planning, especially for non-reasoning models, and extends the Fast Downward superiority claim to V3. The central contribution of reusable domain-dependent heuristics outperforming traditional heuristics remains intact.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning reasoning versus memorization, useful candidate diversity, and imperfect heuristic selection. Section 6 explicitly discusses dependence on PDDL, uncertain generalization, prompt dependence, and implementation constraints. Appendix B additionally explains heuristic behavior and failure mechanisms across six previously undescribed domains.

D1.justification: Appendices A, C, and D add extensive generation, end-to-end, and ablation prompt listings, including example heuristic code and planner structures; embedded PDDL files are abridged. V2 also documents domain parameter ranges, identifies V3 version 0324, specifies training-run memory limits, and supplies a code-and-experiment-data archive reference. These disclosures do not by themselves establish changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion and citations for Tree of Thoughts, Algorithm of Thoughts/AoT+, planning formalization, and supporting theoretical background. It removes Ling et al.'s heuristic-discovery discussion and several broader planning references. The principal positioning relative to Tuisov, Katz, Silver, and FunSearch remains.

P1.justification: The method exposition is substantially condensed, prompt and checklist material is reorganized into Appendix A, and existing heuristic explanations are consolidated in Appendix B. Experimental discussion is reordered, related work is tightened, and a dedicated limitations section and additional appendices substantially restructure the narrative.

P2.justification: V2 expands Tables 2 and 3, adds parameter-range, ablation, and throughput tables, and removes v1's cost/failure table and candidate-count figure. The plan-length/expansion plots are retained and renumbered. Appendix listings are reformatted and expanded, substantially changing the document's visual organization.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens v1's evidence with direct end-to-end baselines, component ablations, and altered/novel-domain tests. Expanded prompt documentation, code/data access information, and explicit limitations also improve reproducibility and critical assessment. These gains outweigh the removed failure-rate and sampling-curve detail, although the new tests provide suggestive rather than conclusive evidence for reasoning over memorization.
